Get A Free Roof Inspection FAQs about Dallas & Fort Worth Roofing​ HOW LONG DO ROOFS LAST? The lifespan of a roof generally ranges from 15 to 30 years, depending on the material used and the level of maintenance it receives. Asphalt shingles, one of the most popular choices for residential roofing, typically last 20 to 25 years. Clay tile roofs can endure 40 to 50 years with proper care, while metal roofing may exceed 40 years, though it can age more quickly in regions with strong sunlight or high winds. Several other factors can shorten a roof’s life, including poor attic ventilation or insulation, improper installation, hail damage, and even damage caused by animals scratching shingles or chewing on deck boards. To maximize the life of your roof, preventive maintenance is key. This includes checking for missing or damaged shingles, cleaning gutters, replacing cracked chimney flashings, fixing rusted metal trim around skylights and vents, and preventing standing water near downspouts, which can lead to wear over time. These proactive measures help protect your home and avoid costly repairs due to neglect. With regular inspections—annually or semi-annually if you live in an area prone to severe weather—you can extend your roof’s lifespan significantly. WHEN IS IT BETTER TO REPLACE A ROOF THAN REPAIR IT? When deciding between repairing or replacing a roof, several factors come into play. The age and current condition of your roof are key considerations. Generally, if your roof is over 20 years old, replacement is often the better option, as repairs may provide only a short-term solution. Major damage, such as holes from weathering or dents from hail, can significantly shorten the life expectancy of your roof and usually calls for a full replacement. This is especially true if there are multiple layers of shingles on your roof. Stacking shingles can increase moisture retention and decrease ventilation, leading to accelerated aging and potential structural issues down the line. Additionally, it’s essential to consider energy efficiency when weighing repair versus replacement; newer roofs often offer better insulation, which can lower heating and cooling costs over time and add value to your property while improving indoor climate control. Considering all these factors is crucial when deciding between repair and replacement, but as a rule of thumb, if a roof is older than 20 years, replacement is usually the preferred choice for its durability and ability to withstand future weather conditions. HOW LONG DOES IT TAKE TO INSTALL A NEW ROOF ON MY HOUSE? The time required to install a new roof depends on several factors, including the size and number of stories of your home, the type of roofing material (such as asphalt shingles or metal), and any unique features that may require additional work. On average, most asphalt shingle roofs can be completed in a single day if the home is single-story. However, for a two-story home or a roof with a complex layout and multiple angles, the installation may take two or more days, depending on the roof’s size and complexity. Metal roofs generally take longer to install than asphalt shingles due to the specialized materials and techniques required. For example, installing a metal roof may involve cutting custom pieces for flashings and valleys, which adds to the time. Beyond the primary installation, additional tasks are often necessary when replacing a roof. These can include removing debris from attic spaces, adding new plywood underlayment over existing layers, installing an ice and water shield around eaves, and placing it along ridges under base flashings. Each of these steps affects the overall timeline for completing a roof installation. For an accurate estimate on how long it will take to install your new roof, consult a reputable local roofing professional. They will evaluate your roof’s current condition and provide a detailed timeline based on your unique needs. IS RESIDENTIAL ROOFING DIFFERENT THAN COMMERCIAL ROOFING? Yes, residential roofing differs significantly from commercial roofing. Commercial roofing typically demands more technical expertise, engineering knowledge, and specialized equipment due to the scale and complexity of the projects. The materials used in commercial roofing are often more costly than those used in residential applications, as they must endure harsher conditions for extended periods, such as intense UV exposure and high winds. Professional installation is essential for commercial roofing systems, often requiring contractors to hold specific certifications or qualifications to be eligible to bid on these projects. This requirement adds another layer of cost compared to residential roofing, which homeowners can sometimes undertake themselves if they choose. HOW OFTEN SHOULD MY ROOF BE INSPECTED? data.summary: The complete absence of customer reviews across all major platforms for an 8-year-old company is a severe red flag. The BBB A+ rating lacks the context of customer reviews or complaint details to validate it. This pattern is highly suspicious and suggests the company may be avoiding public review platforms or has manipulated its online presence.
fake_signals: Zero reviews on all major consumer platforms (Google, Yelp, Angi, Houzz, Trustpilot)
BBB profile shows no customer reviews or complaint details
Company is 8 years old with no public review history, which is highly unusual
authentic_signals: BBB A+ rating exists, but without supporting review data its value is limited
data.discrepancy_explanation: The company has an A+ BBB rating but zero reviews on Google, Yelp, Angi, Houzz, and Trustpilot. This is a major red flag for a company in business for 8 years, as it suggests a lack of public customer feedback or potential review manipulation/avoidance.
